mem.t: But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you won’t fulfill the lust of the flesh.

lessons.title: The Spirit Dwells in the Heart
lessons.theme: My body is the temple of the Holy Spirit; my heart is his home

v: I will also give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you. I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh.
I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes. You will keep my ordinances and do them.
Or don’t you know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God? You are not your own,
for you were bought with a price. Therefore glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God’s.

lessons.still: Sit quietly and notice your breathing. With each breath in, silently say, “Holy Spirit”; with each breath out, “I am yours.” Continue for a minute, reminding yourself that he is not far away in the sky—he lives within me.
teach: A house where the owner has moved in is completely different from a house that merely has the owner’s photo hanging on the wall. Many Christians know that God is “in heaven” but are not aware that God is “within.” One of the most astonishing announcements of the New Testament is that almighty God, by his Holy Spirit, has come to live in our hearts.

Ezekiel prophesied that God would perform a “heart transplant”: taking away the heart of stone, giving a heart of flesh, and “I will put my Spirit within you.” This promise was fulfilled after Pentecost. That is why Paul says, “Your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit.” In the Old Testament, God’s presence dwelt in the temple; in the New Testament, God dwells in believers. The result: “You are not your own,” for we “were bought with a price.”

The Spirit dwells in the heart, not in the head. This is not opposition to thinking; it means that the center of the spiritual life is the heart—the seat of will, emotion and trust. We do not strain with our minds to figure God out; we respond in our hearts to the God who has already moved in. Here is the mindset change: God is not merely someone I study but the Master who lives with me.
lessons.light: 321 Light: One of the three foundations—the Holy Spirit is my guide. Live from the heart by the Spirit, not from the head by yourself; living from the heart brings joy, living from the head brings worry. “You are not your own” is the very foundation of the self-emptied life: I belong to the One who lives within me.
q: Who is God? — God is willing to live in your heart. What does this say about how close he longs to be to you?
Who am I? — Are you more often aware of God “in heaven” or God “within”?
How shall I respond? — How will you glorify the Holy Spirit who lives in you with your body today?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus was baptized, the Holy Spirit descended on him in bodily form like a dove (Luke 3:22). He was full of the Spirit, was led by the Spirit into the wilderness, and returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit (Luke 4:1, 14). Jesus lived a life indwelt and guided by the Spirit, and he promised to give that same Spirit to us.
lessons.pray: Holy Spirit, thank you for living in me and making my body your temple. I am not my own; I was bought with a price. Be Lord in my heart, take away its hardness, and make me willing to follow your guidance. Today I will glorify God in my body. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Three times today, stop and silently say, “Holy Spirit, you are here”
Choose one bodily habit (eating, sleep, what you look at) and adjust it today for the sake of the Spirit’s temple
Write down one area where “I am not my own” needs to become real
lessons.noon: “Or don’t you know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you” — Lord, right now I acknowledge that you live in me.

lessons.title: The Work of the Counselor
lessons.theme: The Holy Spirit is the One beside us who accompanies, teaches and reminds

v: the Spirit of truth, whom the world can’t receive, for it doesn’t see him and doesn’t know him. You know him, for he lives with you and will be in you.
But the Counselor, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you all things, and will remind you of all that I said to you.

lessons.still: Quietly ask the Holy Spirit to remind you of something Jesus said. Don’t rush to look it up; simply wait. If a saying comes to mind, repeat it slowly a few times and thank the Spirit for the reminder.
teach: When someone arrives in an unfamiliar city, if a local friend stays by their side the whole time—showing the way, translating, warning them what not to do—they are no longer a lonely traveler. When Jesus was about to leave his disciples, he did not hand them a manual and walk away. He promised that the Father would give them “another Counselor” to be with them forever.

The word translated “Counselor” means “one called alongside”—a comforter, a helper, an advocate. “Another” means one of the same kind as Jesus: the Holy Spirit is not a force but a personal God. His work includes: he “lives with you,” he “will be in you,” he “will teach you all things,” and he “will remind you of all that I said to you.”

So the Spirit’s work cannot be separated from the words of Jesus. What he reminds us of is what Jesus said; where he leads will never contradict Scripture. The more we hide the word in our hearts, the more “material” the Spirit has to remind us with. Scripture is the standard and the Spirit is the guide; when the two work together, we will not veer to the left or to the right.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The three foundations are bound together—Jesus is my example; Scripture is my standard; the Holy Spirit is my guide. The Spirit always points to Jesus and reminds us of his words. Any “prompting” that exalts the self rather than Jesus needs to be tested by Scripture.
q: Who is God? — The Holy Spirit is “another Counselor.” What is his relationship to Jesus?
Who am I? — Do you often feel like a lonely traveler, forgetting that someone has been beside you all along?
How shall I respond? — How will you pay attention today to the words of Jesus the Spirit brings to mind?
lessons.jesus: While on earth, Jesus personally accompanied, taught and reminded his disciples. Yet he said, “It is to your advantage that I go away” (John 16:7). For after he left, the Holy Spirit could live in every believer, no longer limited by time or place. The presence of the Counselor is the continuation of the presence of Jesus.
lessons.pray: Holy Spirit, our Counselor, thank you for always being with me and living in me. Teach me to understand the truth, and remind me of Jesus’ words when I need them. When I am lonely, confused or weak, let me remember that you are right beside me. I want to learn to hear your voice. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Before reading Scripture, pray, “Holy Spirit, please teach me”
When a verse comes to mind today, write it down and review it in the evening
Send a word of greeting to someone who is lonely, as an instrument of the Spirit’s comfort
lessons.noon: “Will teach you all things” — Lord, right now let your Spirit remind me of your words.

lessons.title: Walking by the Spirit
lessons.theme: Keeping in step with the Spirit naturally bears the fruit of life

v: But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you won’t fulfill the lust of the flesh.
For the flesh lusts against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; and these are contrary to one another, that you may not do the things that you desire.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith,
gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.
Those who belong to Christ have crucified the flesh with its passions and lusts.
If we live by the Spirit, let’s also walk by the Spirit.

lessons.still: Imagine walking side by side with a friend, matching your pace to his—not rushing ahead, not lagging behind. Quietly say to the Holy Spirit, “Today I want to keep in step with you.” Then notice which matter in your heart wants to rush ahead.
teach: In a three-legged race, the key to winning is not who runs fastest but who stays in step. If one person charges off at their own pace, both fall over. When Paul says, “let’s also walk by the Spirit” (verse 25), the word he uses means to fall into line, to march in step—not an occasional sprint, but everyday keeping pace.

Galatians 5 describes a tug-of-war inside us: “the flesh lusts against the Spirit.” The answer is not to clamp down on the flesh by sheer willpower but to “walk by the Spirit, and you won’t fulfill the lust of the flesh”—bring in the light and the darkness retreats on its own. The result is “the fruit of the Spirit.” Notice it is “fruit,” singular: nine qualities like one cluster of grapes, all coming from a single life.

Fruit is not manufactured; it grows. A fruit tree doesn’t have to grit its teeth to produce fruit; it only needs to stay connected to its source of life. If we want love, joy and peace, we don’t “produce” them; we follow the Spirit day by day and let his life flow out naturally. This is the “9” of 920—bearing the ninefold fruit in front of every “2.”
lessons.light: 321 Light: The practice of 920—every person in my life is my “2”; I practise the “0” of the self-emptied life; and the “9” is the ninefold fruit of the Spirit. Those who have crucified the flesh no longer rule themselves but let the Spirit be Lord, and the fruit grows naturally.
q: Who is God? — The fruit of the Spirit is God’s own character. What does it show you about who he is?
Who am I? — Of the nine fruits, which one is most lacking in your life?
How shall I respond? — With which of your “2”s today will you especially follow the Spirit?
lessons.jesus: The ninefold fruit of the Spirit is a portrait of Jesus: love for sinners, joy in the Father, peace in the storm, patience with his disciples, kindness to children, goodness to the oppressed, faithfulness to the Father, gentleness toward people, and self-control in temptation. Bearing fruit means living out Jesus.
lessons.pray: Holy Spirit, I often charge ahead at my own pace, and I fall and get hurt. Today I want to walk by you and keep in step with you. Grow in me love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control—especially the one I lack the most. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Choose the fruit you most lack and deliberately practise it toward one person today
When emotions rise, pause for three seconds and ask, “Holy Spirit, how do you want me to respond?”
Before bed, list the nine fruits and tick the ones you experienced today
lessons.noon: “If we live by the Spirit, let’s also walk by the Spirit.” — Lord, right now I keep in step with you.

lessons.title: Do Not Quench the Spirit
lessons.theme: Be sensitive and responsive to the Spirit; don’t let the fire in your heart go out

v: Test all things, and hold firmly that which is good.
Don’t grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.

lessons.still: Think back to the last time you felt a gentle nudge in your heart—to check on someone, to take back a word, to help with a need. Did you respond? Quietly tell the Lord, “I want to listen and obey you more sensitively.”
teach: A brazier of coals, stirred now and then and fed with fresh charcoal, burns brighter and brighter; douse it with cold water or leave it alone, and soon only ashes remain. When Paul says, “Don’t quench the Spirit,” “quench” means to put out a fire. The Holy Spirit often gives gentle promptings in our hearts; ignore them again and again, and the heart slowly grows cold.

In the same passage Paul gives balance. On one hand, “Don’t quench” and “Don’t despise”; on the other, “Test all things, and hold firmly that which is good.” Not every thought is from the Spirit, so we must test; but neither should we ignore everything for fear of getting it wrong. Ephesians uses relational language: “Don’t grieve the Holy Spirit of God.” The Spirit is a person, and he is grieved by our bitterness, anger and lies.

How can we discern the Spirit’s prompting? It agrees with Scripture, exalts Jesus, and makes us more humble and more loving. It is usually a quiet, clear nudge that brings peace, not panic and condemnation. The best training is “prompt obedience in small things”: if he prompts you to make a phone call, make it; if he prompts you to keep quiet, keep quiet.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The self-ruled person evaluates with the head: “Is this worth it? Will I lose face?”—and so douses the prompting. The self-emptied person responds from the heart to the Spirit and lets him be Lord. Scripture is the standard and the Spirit is the guide: test by Scripture, respond with obedience, and the fire burns ever brighter.
q: Who is God? — The Holy Spirit can be “grieved.” What does this show you about how close his relationship with you is?
Who am I? — Is there a recent prompting that you put out with reasons and excuses?
How shall I respond? — If a small nudge comes today, are you willing to obey right away?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he sees the Father doing” (John 5:19). He was exquisitely sensitive to the Father’s heart: waiting by a well for one woman, stopping in a jostling crowd to ask who had touched him. He never let busyness quench the Father’s promptings.
lessons.pray: Holy Spirit, forgive me for the many times I have doused your promptings with excuses, and for grieving you with bitterness and anger. Kindle the fire in my heart again. Give me wisdom to discern and courage to obey, so that I respond to you at once in small things. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: When you sense a prompting to do good today, act on it within ten minutes
Write down a recent prompting you ignored, confess it to the Lord, and make it right
Before you speak, ask: “Would these words grieve the Holy Spirit?”
lessons.noon: “Don’t quench the Spirit.” — Lord, right now I want to respond to your gentle voice.

lessons.title: Guard Your Heart
lessons.theme: Life flows from the heart; a Spirit-filled heart is a wellspring

v: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.
that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, that you may be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner person,
that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith, to the end that you, being rooted and grounded in love,

lessons.still: Imagine that your heart is a well. Quietly ask the Lord to clear away the debris at its mouth—a worry, a grudge, a craving—taking them out one by one and handing them to him. Then ask the Holy Spirit to rise up like living water from the bottom of the well.
teach: If a river is polluted upstream, the cities downstream will struggle no matter how much they filter; protecting the source is the most fundamental way to protect the whole city. Many people put great effort into managing their words, behavior and image (downstream) but give little care to their own hearts (upstream).

Proverbs says, “Keep your heart with all diligence,” because “out of it is the wellspring of life.” Our words, choices, relationships and ministry all flow from this source. Paul’s prayer for the Ephesians was also about the heart: “that you may be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner person, that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith.” The Spirit works from the inside out.

This week we have seen: the Spirit dwells in the heart → the Counselor accompanies and teaches → walking by the Spirit → not quenching the Spirit → and today, guarding this heart in which the Spirit lives. A heart ruled by the Spirit naturally pours out self-giving love. Next week we will learn Jesus’ way of self-denial: living for Jesus and for others.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Life flows from the heart—live from the heart by the Spirit, not from the head by yourself. Transformation begins in the heart: when the heart changes, lifestyle, relationships and ministry change with it. Life first, then relationships, then ministry; guarding the heart is guarding the source of all of these.
q: Who is God? — Why does God care most about your heart rather than your outward performance?
Who am I? — What is polluting your “upstream” right now?
How shall I respond? — How will you guard your heart today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “Out of the abundance of the heart, the mouth speaks” (Matthew 12:34). He rebuked the Pharisees for cleaning the outside of the cup and plate while inside they were full of extortion and self-indulgence (Matthew 23:25). Jesus always cares about the heart, because he renews a person from the heart outward.
lessons.pray: Lord, search my heart and remove the pollution within. I want to guard my heart above all else. Strengthen me with power through your Spirit in my inner being, so that Christ may dwell in my heart through faith. May my words, choices and relationships all flow from a heart filled with you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Review three kinds of information that entered your heart today, and cut out one that does not build you up
Before starting each task, silently pray, “Lord, guard my heart”
Share with a spiritual companion one reminder the Holy Spirit gave you this week
lessons.noon: “Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.” — Lord, right now I give my heart to you to guard.
